one_liner: Community chat platform with bots, messaging, voice, and app integrations

evidence.claim: Two authentication methods: bot tokens and OAuth2 bearer tokens, sent in the Authorization header
evidence.quote: For all authentication types, authentication is performed with the `Authorization` HTTP header in the format `Authorization: TOKEN_TYPE TOKEN`.

evidence.claim: Self-serve OAuth2 credentials via the public Developer Portal
evidence.quote: The first step in implementing OAuth2 is [registering a developer application](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and retrieving your client ID and client secret.

evidence.claim: Bot tokens are generated self-serve from the app's Bot settings page
evidence.quote: On the [**Bot** page](https://discord.com/developers/applications/select/bot) under **Token**, click "Reset Token" to generate a new bot token.
The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.

evidence.claim: Broad API surface covering channels, guilds, users, and messages
evidence.quote: interact and modify core Discord resources like [channels](/developers/resources/channel), [servers (or guilds)](/developers/resources/guild)

notes: No official Discord MCP server; mcp.dis.gg is a third-party hosted MCP wrapping bot tokens. A bidirectional WebSocket Gateway API complements REST for real-time events. Some OAuth2 scopes (e.g., identify.premium) are partner-only, and privileged Gateway intents require approval after app verification, but core API access is fully self-serve. Token endpoints accept only application/x-www-form-urlencoded, not JSON. An official OpenAPI 3.1 spec is published at github.com/discord/discord-api-spec. Bot tokens use the 'Bot' prefix rather than 'Bearer'.
